tldr: This is a loose thread of three separate projects, not one event: each tries to run inference on GPUs beyond a single CUDA stack. Google opened it with ML Drift, an Apache 2.0 engine for on-device inference across GPU vendors, and a small C++/HIP inference server for AMD GPUs followed on Codeberg.
whats_new: A pull request to the open-source project-maya adds combined CUDA and ROCm backends so one LLM inference job can span NVIDIA and AMD GPUs; its title claims up to 48% faster, with no independent benchmark yet.
why_it_matters: Inference that runs on more than one GPU vendor gives teams leverage on hardware cost and supply, but these projects are early and their performance numbers are self-reported.

beats.headline: Google open-sources ML Drift for on-device inference across GPUs
beats.summary: A first-party GPU compute engine that hides vendor differences for on-device ML inference.

beats.headline: A C++/HIP inference server targets AMD GPUs directly
beats.summary: A small independent project skips CUDA and writes the server against AMD's HIP API.

beats.headline: Dual CUDA+ROCm backend PR claims up to 48% faster mixed-vendor inference
beats.summary: An open pull request, not a release; the speedup comes from the PR title alone.

open_questions: Does the project-maya CUDA+ROCm pull request merge, and what workload and baseline produce the 48% figure?
Does an independent benchmark compare mixed NVIDIA+AMD inference against a single-vendor setup at equal cost?
Does ML Drift add server-side or LLM-scale support, or stay on-device only?
Does the AMD HIP inference server publish throughput and model-support numbers against vLLM on ROCm?
take_for_builders: Treat these as experiments: rerun your own latency and throughput evals on mixed or AMD hardware before you plan capacity around them, and keep your CUDA serving path as the fallback.
